CLASS IDENTITY IS THE CARTRIDGE'S, NOT A COINED ONE. _ZTS at ov017:0x02111bc0 spells "14daObjKsWater_c"; _ZTI at 0x02111bb4 is an __si_class_type_info whose +8 word points at _ZTI10dBgActor_c (ov002:0x021089ec), so the direct base is dBgActor_c and nothing else; _ZTV at 0x02111bf8 is the address point, with a zero offset-to-top and &_ZTI in the two words below it at 0x02111bf0. The former coined ShipWater spelling has been removed from config/arm9/overlays/ov017/symbols.txt (it duplicated _ZTV14daObjKsWater_c on the same word) and renamed out of the tree with tools/class_rename.py.

THE DESTRUCTOR IS DECLARED FIRST AND INLINE, which is the opposite of what ov029/daObjWc_Mizu_c needed and for a different reason. There, no TU defined the destructor as a C++ member at all, so declaring it last was the only way to make mwccarm emit the RTTI anywhere. Here the inline definition IS the key function: this TU defines all six of the class's virtuals, mwccarm homes _ZTV/_ZTI/_ZTS here, and the eleven records are licensed below. Declaring it out of line instead makes mwccarm emit D0 ahead of D1 -- the cartridge has D1 first at 0x021111a0 -- which objisolate refuses with `requested functions are not emitted in ROM order`, and adds an unhomed D2 the ROM never carried.

THE VPTR STORE CARRIES THE +8 BIAS. Because this TU emits the vtable rather than importing it, `_ZTV14daObjKsWater_c` names the emitted OBJECT -- the two-word Itanium preamble at 0x02111bf0 -- so daObjKsWater_c_classInit stores `&_ZTV14daObjKsWater_c[2]`, which lands on 0x02111bf8, the word the cartridge actually writes. A plain addend-0 reference would be eight bytes low.

decl_common.h is deliberately not included by this TU: it declares data_ov017_02111c88 as an int array, and the TU needs it at its real SharedFilePtr type to call Release(). The one declaration the factory block would have taken from it, the vtable array, is restated in the file.
